subject.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use and narrow catch

question: Should plugin-runtime callers fail closed on every legacy ownerless parent or target session, or must upgrades provide an explicit migration or recovery path before enforcing exact owner equality?
rationale: Both choices affect a security boundary and existing persisted sessions: allowing ownerless access preserves compatibility but permits ambiguous authority, while unconditional rejection may break existing plugin workflows without an operator-facing recovery path.

options.title: Fail closed now
options.body: Reject ownerless rows for plugin-runtime callers across create, patch, delete, takeover, and reset, accepting the compatibility break to preserve an unambiguous security boundary.

options.title: Add migration path
options.body: Keep the strict runtime rule but first provide a bounded doctor or operator recovery flow that assigns or replaces legacy ownerless plugin sessions.

options.title: Preserve legacy access
options.body: Allow ownerless rows temporarily with a documented deprecation window, reducing upgrade breakage while retaining ambiguous plugin authority.

recommendation.title: Fail closed now
recommendation.body: Reject ownerless rows for plugin-runtime callers across create, patch, delete, takeover, and reset, accepting the compatibility break to preserve an unambiguous security boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing review discussion identifies this person as the best available routing candidate for the ownerless-session policy choice.
